Gandhiji’s next activity was in 1918 at Ahmedabad where agitation was going on between the industrial workers and the owners of a cotton textile mill for the Plague bonus. While Gandhiji was negotiating with the mill owners, he advised the workers to go on strike and to demand 35% increase Plague Bonus. Naturally, the development of the country depends on the development of villages. That is why Gandhi stressed on the growth of rural industries such as khadi, handlooms, sericulture, handicrafts, etc. Rural industries are based on family labour and require less amount of capital.
